newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power mostly softer on mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power mostly softer on mild weather.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. were mostly weaker Wednesday, pressured by a fairly weak demand because of the mild temperatures now in the region, sources said.

Firm, peak power prices in the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Thursday were sharply lower in the $15.50-16.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, down from the $21.00-22.00 area seen on Tuesday.
Firm, off-peak electricity in northern TVA was notionally assessed around $12.50, down about $2 from Tuesday.
"There's just no demand. The buyers are disappearing," one market source said, adding softer prices in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) were contributing to the downtrend.
Next-day peak, firm prices in SPP were talked in the $16.00-17.00 per MWh range.

At the Georgia/Florida border, prices for firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks for Thursday delivery were steady to softer in the $23.00-24.00 per MWh range, as compared with Tuesday's $23.50-$24.00 trading range.
Firm, off-peak power for Thursday at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally assessed at $16.00.

Despite the softness throughout most of the Southeastern Electric Reliability Council (SERC) territory, hourly prices in Florida were heard as high as $50 per MWh due to reports of some coal plant outages.
Firm power in Florida on a 12-hour schedule sold in the $23.00-26.00 range, while 16-hour power prices were talked in the $23.00-24.00 area.
Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to remain warm Thursday and Friday but then fall to normal to slightly below-normal levels this weekend.
Separately, Southern Co's 822 megawatt Farley 2 nuclear power unit in Dothan, Ala., is scheduled to restart on December 15 after being shut October 12 for refueling and maintenance.
